Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP701 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Reversed Carnot COP: $COP_{\text{Carnot}} = \frac{T_e}{T_c - T_e} = \frac{T_L}{T_H - T_L}$ (Temperatures strictly in Kelvin)
  • Bell-Coleman Cycle COP: $COP_{\text{air}} = \frac{1}{r_p^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma} - 1}$ (where $r_p = p_2/p_1$)
  • Refrigerant Chemical Nomenclature: For $R-(m-1)(n+1)(p)$: $C_m H_n F_p Cl_q$ where $2m + 2 = n + p + q$ (e.g. $R134a \implies CH_2FCF_3$)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Desirable Refrigerant Qualities: High latent heat of vaporization, low boiling point, non-toxic, non-flammable, zero ODP (Ozone Depletion Potential), low GWP (Global Warming Potential).
  • Natural Refrigerants: Ammonia ($R717$ - high efficiency, toxic), Carbon dioxide ($R744$ - transcritical), Hydrocarbons (Isobutane $R600a$, Propane $R290$).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs/HCFCs; Kigali Amendment mandates HFC phase-down.
  • Air refrigeration has low COP (~1.2-1.5) but is universally used in aircraft air-conditioning due to ultralight air-cycle machines.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Refrigeration Fundamentals & Fluid Dynamics

1. Gas Cycle Refrigeration & Environmental Thermodynamics

Gas cycles use non-condensing gas (air) where isentropic expansion in a turbo-expander produces cryogenic sub-zero supply air. ASHRAE standard refrigerant classification balances safety (A1 non-toxic non-flammable vs A3/B2) with atmospheric lifecycle degradation.

$$R-(c-1)(h+1)f \implies R11: CCl_3F, \quad R12: CCl_2F_2, \quad R22: CHClF_2, \quad R134a: CF_3CH_2F$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Aircraft passenger cabin environmental control systems (ECS) and commercial cold chains.

Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP701 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Optimum Intermediate Pressure: $p_i = \sqrt{p_c \cdot p_e}$ (Geometric mean minimizing total multi-stage compressor work)
  • Multi-Stage Power Saving: Intercooling desuperheats LP discharge before entering HP stage, reducing specific volume and compression work.
  • Flash Chamber Gas Separation: Vapour flashed during throttling is bypassed directly to HP stage, reducing mass flow handled by LP compressor.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Cascade Refrigeration: Two independent circuits using different refrigerants (e.g. R404A in high stage, R23 in low stage) operating across cascade condenser.
  • Volumetric Efficiency ($\eta_v$): $\eta_v = 1 + C - C\left(\frac{p_c}{p_e}\right)^{1/n}$ (Clearance ratio $C = V_c / V_s$).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • High pressure ratios ($p_c / p_e > 6$) degrade single-stage volumetric efficiency drastically, requiring multi-staging.
  • Cascade systems reach temperatures below -80°C for biomedical vaccine and plasma cryopreservation.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Compound Vapour Compression Engineering

1. Multi-Pressure Compression & Flash Economizers

For large temperature lifts between -40°C evaporator and +45°C ambient condenser, single-stage compressors overheat and deliver poor volumetric efficiency. Staging with flash gas removal maximizes Carnot COP.

$$W_{\text{total}} = \dot{m}_1 (h_2 - h_1) + \dot{m}_2 (h_4 - h_3), \quad \text{COP} = \frac{\dot{m}_1 (h_1 - h_8)}{W_{\text{total}}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Industrial ice manufacturing plants, deep-freeze seafood trawlers, and blast freezers.

<svg viewBox="0 0 500 150" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Water-Ammonia (NH₃-H₂O) VARS Energy Loop</text>
  <rect x="70" y="55" width="80" height="40" fill="#ef4444" rx="4"/>
  <text x="80" y="80" fill="#fff" font-size="10">Generator (Qg)</text>
  <line x1="150" y1="75" x2="230" y2="75" stroke="#f59e0b" stroke-width="2"/>
  <rect x="230" y="55" width="80" height="40" fill="#3b82f6" rx="4"/>
  <text x="240" y="80" fill="#fff" font-size="10">Condenser</text>
  <rect x="150" y="105" width="80" height="35" fill="#10b981" rx="4"/>
  <text x="160" y="127" fill="#fff" font-size="10">Absorber (Qa)</text>
  <text x="330" y="85" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="11">COP = (Qe/Qg) = [Te/(Tc-Te)] · [(Tg-Tc)/Tg]</text>
</svg>
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP701 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Maximum Theoretical VARS COP: $COP_{\max} = \left( \frac{T_e}{T_c - T_e} \right) \left( \frac{T_g - T_c}{T_g} \right) = COP_{\text{Carnot}} \times \eta_{\text{Carnot Engine}}$
  • Refrigerant-Absorbent Pairs: NH3-H2O (Ammonia is refrigerant, water is absorbent; suitable for sub-zero cooling); H2O-LiBr (Water is refrigerant, LiBr is absorbent; air-conditioning >0°C).
  • Mechanical Pump Work: Liquid solution pump consumes negligible electrical power (<2% of mechanical compressor).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • VARS Key Components: Generator (heat input), Condenser, Expansion valve, Evaporator, Absorber (heat rejection), Solution pump, Heat exchanger, Rectifier/Analyser.
  • Three-Fluid System (Electrolux): Uses Hydrogen (inert gas) to lower ammonia partial pressure without any mechanical pump (hermetically sealed, silent).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • H2O-LiBr cannot operate below 0°C because water would freeze into solid ice in evaporator tubes.
  • Ideal for waste heat utilization from diesel generator exhaust or solar thermal parabolic collectors.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Thermal Absorption & Waste Heat Cooling

1. Thermo-Chemical Absorption Cycles

Compressor is replaced by thermal compressor consisting of absorber, low-power liquid pump, and thermal generator. High-grade electrical work is replaced by low-grade thermal energy $Q_g$.

$$COP = \frac{Q_e}{Q_g + W_p} \approx \frac{Q_e}{Q_g}, \quad COP_{\text{actual}} \approx 0.6 - 0.8 \text{ (Single-effect)}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Solar-powered decentralized cold storage and co-generation tri-generation plants.

Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP701 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Room Sensible Heat Factor (RSHF): $RSHF = \frac{RSH}{RSH + RLH}$
  • Grand Sensible Heat Factor (GSHF): $GSHF = \frac{TSH}{TSH + TLH} = \frac{RSH + OASH}{(RSH+OASH) + (RLH+OALH)}$
  • Dehumidified Air Quantity: $\dot{V}_{cmm} = \frac{RSH}{0.0204 (T_{\text{room}} - T_{\text{supply}})}$ (m³/min)
  • Apparatus Dew Point (ADP): Effective surface temperature of cooling coil where the RSHF line intersects saturation curve.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Coil Bypass Factor ($BPF$): $BPF = \frac{T_{\text{off}} - T_{\text{adp}}}{T_{\text{on}} - T_{\text{adp}}}$, Contact factor $\eta = 1 - BPF$.
  • Ventilation Air Load (OASH/OALH): Outside fresh air introduces sensible and latent loads based on occupancy standards (ASHRAE 62.1).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Slope of RSHF line on psychrometric chart determines required supply air temperature.
  • Reheat coil is necessary when cooling and dehumidification overcools air below thermal comfort limits.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Psychrometric System Engineering & Load Estimation

1. Building Thermal Load Formulations & Coil Psychrometry

Total heat gain encompasses solar radiation through fenestrations (SHGC), conduction through building envelope, internal sensible gains from occupants and equipment, and latent moisture infiltration.

$$Q_{\text{envelope}} = U A \Delta T_{\text{eq}}, \quad Q_{\text{solar}} = A \cdot SC \cdot SHGF, \quad Q_{\text{vent}} = 1.2 \dot{V} \Delta h$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Commercial IT park central air conditioning and hospital infection control isolation wards.

Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP701 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Circular Equivalent of Rectangular Duct: $D_{eq} = 1.30 \frac{(a \cdot b)^{0.625}}{(a + b)^{0.25}}$ (Equal friction and capacity)
  • Duct Friction Pressure Drop (Darcy): $\Delta p_f = f \frac{L}{D} \frac{\rho v^2}{2}$
  • Thermal Comfort Indices (Fanger): Predicted Mean Vote (PMV, -3 cold to +3 hot) and Predicted Percentage of Dissatisfied (PPD $\le 10\%$ for ASHRAE 55).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Duct Design Methods: Equal Friction method (constant pressure drop per meter, e.g. 0.8-1.0 Pa/m); Static Regain method (velocity reduced after branch to recover static pressure).
  • Air Distribution Systems: Constant Air Volume (CAV) vs Variable Air Volume (VAV with pressure-independent dampers); All-water vs All-air systems.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Aspect ratio of rectangular ducts should ideally be below 4:1 to prevent excessive friction and sheet metal vibration.
  • Thermal comfort factors: Dry bulb temp, relative humidity, air velocity, mean radiant temperature, clothing insulation (clo), and metabolic rate (met).
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Air Distribution & HVAC Fluid Mechanics

1. Aerodynamic Duct Network Analysis & Static Regain

Designing air distribution requires balancing fan total pressure against linear friction losses and dynamic fitting losses (elbows, transitions, diffusers). Static regain method ensures uniform diffuser discharge pressures throughout building risers.

$$\Delta p_{\text{dynamic}} = C_o \left( \frac{\rho v^2}{2} \right), \quad \Delta p_s = R (v_1^2 - v_2^2) \frac{\rho}{2} - \Delta p_f$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Underfloor air distribution (UFAD) in data centers and high-velocity acoustic ductwork in cinema auditoriums.
